newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates jump with few offering liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates jump with few offering liquidity.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose strongly in early afternoon trade on Monday with the some players nervous about liquidity, dealers said.

"There is no real explanation for the sudden rise of call money," said one dealer, adding some participants were only panicking as they would have to pay 4.5 percent to the central bank if their cash reserve facilities show a negative balance at the end of the trading day.
"Call money was bid around 3.12 to 3.18 at the open, but later some players were willing to pay as much as 4.00 percent," a dealer said, adding one trade was done at 4.25 percent.
The dealer added there was enough liquidity in the market, but players were very cautious and would not bring their surplus into the market before they were sure of their own balance.

The dealer said the new monetary intruments introduced by the central bank last May gave the central bank a stronger grip on the market. But he said it made it more difficult for commercial banks as they were no longer allowed to show a deficit at the end of the day.
"Call money will probably be back at the level of about 3.18 percent bid at the open on Tuesday," the dealer said. Another said the same problem could occur later on during the session.
Deposits were trading at a slightly higher level because of the strong rise in call money rates.
One-month deposits were bidding two basis points higher at 3.12 percent. Three-month deposits also rose two basis points, to 3.16 percent.
The guilder was a touch stronger versus the German mark at 112.580 per 100 marks compared to 112.585 on Friday.
The dollar was firmer and traded above the 2.00 guilder level.
